transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is that over the past year or so, I just feel like I’m always doing something—puttering around, fixing things, arranging things, or saying yes to one more volunteer thing. Even at my age, I have a hard time just sitting down and being still.
During these times when you’re always doing something, do you also feel unusually energetic or high?
I don’t know that I’d call it unusually high. I’m busy, and I feel driven to keep moving, but it doesn’t feel like I’m on top of the world or anything like that. Just… restless, I suppose.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about everyday things?
I’m not sure I’d say I worry a lot. I mean, I have the usual concerns day to day, but I haven’t really noticed constant worrying as the main thing.
Have you been this restless and always-on-the-go since you were a child?

Yes, I think so. I remember even in grade school getting scolded for popping out of my seat or talking over the other children. Teachers would say I was “too lively,” and that was well before I was a teenager.
Do you often have trouble keeping your things or your activities organized?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I try to keep things in their usual places, but I haven’t thought of organization as one of my main problems. What do you mean by activities organized?
Do you often spend so much time trying to do things exactly right that it makes it hard to finish them?
No, I don’t think so. I’m not usually stuck trying to make things perfect. If anything, I just do things the way I can and move on.
